findings.evidence: features/005-scope-change-skill/005-scope-change-skill-prd.md:R3 + R4 + R5 — R3 specifies append-only interview extension with the original Goal/Original Request/Codebase context/prior Rounds 'NEVER edited'. R4 specifies that prior Resolved lines, when explicitly invalidated, are marked with `~~text~~` strikethrough plus a `(superseded by Scope change {date})` note. R5 specifies surgical PRD synthesis where 'only the requirements/ACs whose Trace lines reference the new scope-change rounds (or whose original Trace line is now strikethrough-superseded) are modified'. The unstated load-bearing assumption: the surgical-edit logic in R5 keys off the strikethrough markup in the interview as a machine-readable signal — 'Trace line is now strikethrough-superseded' is treated as a deterministic predicate. But R4 only specifies that strikethrough wraps 'only the affected text, not the whole line' — the markup discipline is human-readable but never formally specified as a parser contract. A future re-fired `specflow:prd` Phase C reading the interview to compute the changed-R-ID set must parse `~~...~~` runs inside Resolved lines and map them back to specific Trace anchors (round-N.line-M). The PRD does not name the load-bearing assumption that (a) strikethrough markup is the canonical signal, (b) Phase C synthesis can reliably extract `(superseded by Scope change {date})` notes as the supersession trigger, and (c) the line-number references in R10.1's `superseded_resolved_lines: [round-2.line-78, ...]` field stay stable across the strikethrough edit (line numbers shift if the strikethrough adds characters mid-line).
findings.claim: Unstated load-bearing assumption — R4's strikethrough markup is treated as a parseable contract by R5's surgical-PRD-synthesis step and R10.1's `superseded_resolved_lines` reference list, but the PRD never states that the markup IS the contract. A Phase C re-fire that misses a strikethrough run, or a `superseded_resolved_lines` entry whose line-number drifted because the strikethrough added 30+ characters to the line, would silently produce a non-surgical PRD diff or a broken decision-log reference. The tradeoff between 'human-readable inline markup' (R4 chose this) and 'machine-parseable structured signal' (e.g. a separate `superseded` block at the end of the round, or an explicit `<sup id=...>` anchor) is not articulated. Round 2 of the interview (line 44) records the user's preference for inline strikethrough so 'a diff viewer shows exactly which characters were marked superseded' — that's the design intent, but the parser-contract corollary is never named.
findings.proposed_change: Sharpen R4 to explicitly name strikethrough markup as the canonical machine-readable signal for supersession, AND tighten R10.1's `superseded_resolved_lines` reference shape to be drift-resistant. Concrete edit: add to R4: 'The `~~text~~` strikethrough markup IS the canonical machine-readable signal for supersession — `specflow:prd` Phase C synthesis (R5) and `specflow:decision` invocation (R10.1) both parse Resolved lines for `~~...~~` runs paired with `(superseded by Scope change {YYYY-MM-DD})` notes; the parenthetical date is the supersession-event anchor.' Change R10.1's `superseded_resolved_lines` shape from line-number references to round-and-anchor-text references: e.g. `superseded_resolved_lines: [{round: 2, anchor: "foo flag defaults to true"}, ...]` — anchor text is byte-stable across strikethrough edits because the strikethrough wraps the original characters, not new ones. Update AC-4 to verify the markup-as-contract: 'AC-4 additionally verifies that every `~~...~~` run inside a Resolved line has a matching `(superseded by Scope change {YYYY-MM-DD})` note within the same line; runs without a matching note are a failed step (i).'
